sentences.text: In September 1945, Sài Gòn was tense.
British troops had arrived to disarm the Japanese, and French soldiers who had been held as prisoners were given weapons again.
On 22 September, French forces opened fire on offices of the southern government, including the post office and the radio station.
On 23 September, with British help, they pushed Vietnamese forces out of Sài Gòn.

On the morning of 23 September, leaders of the southern Party committee, the People's Committee and the Resistance Committee met in a house on Cây Mai Street (today Nguyễn Trãi Street, District 5) and approved a call to resist.
Since then, 23 September has been remembered as Nam Bộ Resistance Day.
It was the start of fighting in the South, but not yet the nationwide war, which began in December 1946.
